app.title: torchseed — graphical configuration builder for torchtree
app.summary: A person loads a sequence alignment, can optionally attach a sampling date to each sequence, and loads a starting tree. With dates in place they can run a root-to-tip regression to check for clock-like signal. They then work through numbered tabs to pick the substitution and site models, the clock model, a tree prior and a prior for each estimated parameter, then the variational family and optimiser settings. Finally they generate the full analysis configuration, preview it with a summary of its components, and download it as a JSON file to run in the inference engine.

task.text: Specify a Bayesian phylogenetic analysis (data, model components, priors and variational inference settings) and export it as a ready-to-run configuration file.

data.text: A multiple sequence alignment of DNA or protein, optional sampling dates per sequence from the names or a CSV, a starting tree in Newick or NEXUS, and a registry of model parameters, each with a starting value, constraint, prior and variational family.
data.item: an estimated model parameter with its starting value, prior and variational distribution

stage.text: setting up a phylogenetic inference run once the alignment and tree exist, before running it

mechanism.text: Numbered tabs act as a wizard: each tab is a form that writes to one shared parameter registry, and later tabs stay locked until an alignment and tree are loaded. The output tab assembles the registry into a JSON configuration to preview and download, while dialogs, plots and tables along the way let the person check the inputs (alignment, tree, dates, root-to-tip fit, rate categories).

field.text: Bayesian phylogenetic inference with molecular clocks and coalescent priors, fitted by variational inference, in evolutionary biology

workflow.name: specify a statistical model step by step and export it as a run configuration

steps.here: Upload a FASTA alignment, choose DNA or Protein in an import dialog, and see it as a row (taxa, sites, type) that can be opened in an alignment viewer or deleted.

steps.step: attach a time to each item
steps.here: Turn on tip dates and parse them from taxon names with a regex or from a CSV with strain and date columns, set the time direction, then check coverage, a date and height table and a histogram with a bin slider.

steps.step: bring in the starting structure and check its signal
steps.here: Upload a Newick or NEXUS tree, view it, and run root-to-tip regression (maximise r² or minimise SSR over every possible root) to read the rate, TMRCA and r² next to a date vs distance scatter plot.

steps.step: choose model components and their parameters
steps.here: Pick a substitution model, which shows its rate matrix, plus Weibull rate categories, invariant sites and a strict or per-branch clock. Each free parameter shows up as a row with a starting value and an estimate checkbox.

steps.step: set a prior on each estimated parameter
steps.here: Choose a coalescent tree prior, then for each estimated parameter pick a distribution and hyperparameters. A hyperparameter can be promoted to an estimated parameter with its own prior, or a prior can be removed.

Pick a variational family per parameter (shown with its transform to unconstrained space), set the time-tree reparameterisation, the objective, optimiser, learning rate, iterations, convergence tolerance and output file stem.
Generate / Refresh JSON assembles the config or reports what is missing, then it shows a JSON preview and a table of component ids and types, with a download button for <stem>.json.

distinctive: Each parameter's constraint (positive, shifted positive, unit interval, simplex, real) decides which priors and variational families are offered and which transform and Jacobian enter the config.
Turning on tip dates switches the analysis from an unrooted tree to a time tree, which unlocks the clock and coalescent models and sets the root height's lower bound to the span of the dates.
A root-to-tip regression searches every edge for the best root to check clock-like signal before the model is specified.
Hyperparameters of a prior can be promoted to estimated parameters with their own priors, and these links survive when the model is changed.
